statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. NQ has now held the 29,530.50-29,596.00 restart band for a fifth hour and last printed 29,565.25, exactly Friday's settle, while the Nikkei extended its advance to +2.30%. An index that widens its range by less than a point over an hour and declines to follow a 2% regional technology rally is rotating, not trending, so Tail remains at the low-band floor. Stress stays elevated on a war-premium energy complex, a restrictive Treasury curve with a close-to-even September policy debate, and a holiday-thinned Monday that halts early.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 15:00-17:00 UTC window covering the European cash close into the early Labor Day futures halt, and secondarily in the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date, rather than across the whole outlook. Every forecast hour maps below the block threshold. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a 65-point restart band for a fifth hour at Friday's settle as a 2.3% Nikkei rally and a contained oil response fail to produce directional structure
body:
The Sunday restart is now roughly five and a half hours old and the observed price path still has not extended. NQ front-month last printed 29,565.25, identical to Friday's 4 September settle, inside a session range of 29,530.50 to 29,596.00. That range is about 65 points, or 0.22%, and it widened by only three quarters of a point over the past hour. A band that stops widening while time passes is the signature of orderly two-way price discovery rather than the directional efficiency that overwhelms mean reversion, and it remains the single most important observation in this assessment.

The divergence that did not transmit has become more pronounced. The Nikkei 225 is now up 2.30% at 66,518 with Tokyo Electron, Advantest and SoftBank leading, echoing Friday's US semiconductor strength where the whole chip complex closed higher. NQ has not followed. An index that declines to track a widening regional technology rally is rotating rather than trending, and rotation is the environment in which mean reversion works.

The weekend geopolitical escalation remains contained. US Central Command struck three Iranian oil tankers in the Gulf of Oman and near Kharg Island on 5 September after the Revolutionary Guard fired ballistic missiles at two US Navy vessels, and Iran said it had targeted tankers in response. WTI trades at 92.03 and Brent at 96.78, up 0.60% and 0.52%, and seven OPEC+ producers separately left October quotas unchanged at about 31.1 million barrels per day at a virtual meeting on 6 September, with the next review set for 4 October. Both benchmarks were already war-elevated from roughly $70 before the strait was effectively closed in February, so this reads as a chronic and largely priced conflict rather than a fresh discontinuity. That is why the escalation supports Stress and not Tail.

Cross-asset alignment is absent. Friday's VIX close of 14.53 is low in absolute terms, the H.15 curve is restrictive but stable with the two-year at 4.34% and the ten-year at 4.77% as of 3 September, and the delayed cross-asset context shows index, rate, gold and volatility futures all within roughly half a percent of unchanged. Friday's Nasdaq internals were split rather than aligned: the semiconductor complex was uniformly higher, led by Micron and AMD, while five of eight megacaps fell and Tesla dropped almost 6%. No shallow-pullback pattern, failed retracement or extreme-holding behaviour has been observed since the restart, so Tail sits at the low-band floor.

Today is Labor Day. US cash equity markets are closed and CME equity index futures trade a shortened session that halts at 17:00 UTC with no Monday settlement published, reopening at 22:00 UTC for the Tuesday trade date. The narrow danger window is placed at 15:00 to 17:00 UTC, covering the European cash close into that hard deadline, because a squeeze into a fixed halt in an already thin book is the most plausible unrepaired-move mechanism in this outlook. It remains a conditional scenario rather than an observation.

The week itself is back-loaded. There is no US release today. August PPI and jobless claims arrive on Thursday 10 September and August CPI on Friday 11 September, the last inflation reading before the 15-16 September FOMC decision, with the Fed already in its pre-meeting communications blackout. Market pricing for that decision is close to evenly split between a quarter-point hike and no change. Under the standing calibration, event importance and forecast dispersion of that kind raise Stress and shape Confidence rather than Tail, and none of those events falls inside this 24-hour outlook.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available; the 21:00 UTC hour on 6 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable with null fields. Tail held a flat 5 through the closed-venue Sunday hours, apart from a single 4 at 02:00 UTC, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout, then stepped to 8 at the 22:00 UTC restart hour to carry reopen-gap risk before easing to 6 and back to 5 once the restart proved orderly. Stress ran from 53 through a 52-58 band to a 60 high at 20:00 UTC as Sunday's geopolitical flow accumulated, then eased to 57, 56, 55 and 54 after the reopen. Dominant mode was normal in every available hour.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover the remainder of the Sunday restart, the rest of the Asian session, a European session traded against a closed US market on Labor Day, a shortened futures session that halts at 17:00 UTC, five closed hours, and the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band for every hour: 5 through the Asian hours now that the restart has proved contained, 6 from the Asian close through the European pre-open, 7 across the European open and morning where the weekend Iran headlines first meet real depth without a US cash backstop, 6 to 7 through the holiday-thinned midday, 8 as the danger window opens at the European cash close and a peak of 9 in the final hour before the early halt, the closed-venue floor of 5 while futures are shut, then 8 at the Tuesday restart easing to 7 and 6. Conditional Stress tracks the same shape between 54 and 58, and Confidence decays from 86 to 74 across the outlook as the assessment ages away from its evidence cutoff.
